app.name: Civic Voice
app.tagline: Enroll once, sign in seconds. No re-issuing your QES on every click, no individual tax number on-chain.

landing.hero: Anonymous, private voting of verified citizens with results in a public blockchain — impossible to delete or falsify.
landing.sub: Discover the opinion of verified citizens on the issue that interests you! Vote and create polls. Each participant uses QES to confirm they are an adult citizen. Personal data stays on your device. Your vote is private — even the registry doesn't know how you voted. Voting results are available in a public distributed registry (blockchain) — without the possibility of deletion or falsification.
landing.subAvailAfter: who use a qualified electronic signature (QES).
landing.eidasNote: Demo version of the site works for voting in Ukraine.
landing.howTitle: Four steps from idea to community opinion.
landing.step1body: Get verified using QES once. Your personal data never leaves your device and is never transmitted anywhere.
landing.step2body: Create polls to discover public opinion from people who have proven they are adult citizens. Participate in polls created by others.
landing.step3title: Anonymity and privacy of identity. Publicity and transparency of results.
landing.step3body: You vote privately. The service doesn't know who you are or how you voted. Voting results are available in a public blockchain (distributed registry) without revealing who voted for what. Data in the registry cannot be deleted or falsified.
landing.step4body: When the vote count reaches the threshold, the poll closes. Results carry no legal consequences and only reflect the opinion of the verified community on a given issue.
landing.transparencyTitle: What data goes to the registry
landing.tech1body: A qualified electronic signature valid in Ukraine and 27 EU countries. Allows identity verification.
landing.tech2body: Technology transforms your personal data and voting result into encrypted mathematical proofs so nobody can find out who you are or what you voted for.
landing.tech3body: Votes are stored in a public blockchain. You see only results, without names of who voted for what. Data in the blockchain cannot be deleted or altered.
landing.tech4body: The project's code is open, which means you can verify that the system works as promised.

enroll.heading: v2 enrollment
enroll.intro: Done once. You prove your identity with a QES, bind it to a Passkey on this device, and from then on every vote is a sub-second tap — no fresh KEP.

binding.title: File to sign in Diia
binding.intro: Before uploading anything, download this small file and sign it inside the Diia app via «Накласти КЕП». Diia produces a .p7s — the file you upload in the next step. The binding scopes your signature to a v2 enrollment intent for today's epoch so the same .p7s cannot be reused as a generic Diia signature elsewhere.
binding.afterDownload: File saved. Open it in Diia: «Документи» → «Накласти КЕП» → select this file → save the resulting .p7s and drag it into step 1.
binding.details: The file is 28 bytes: 20 bytes of the ASCII label `CRISP_QES_V2_ENROLL::`, then an 8-byte big-endian Unix-day index. Diia computes sha256 over those bytes and writes the result as `messageDigest` inside `signedAttrs` in your .p7s. In v2.1 the OPRF service verifies the Diia cert chain but does not yet pin `messageDigest` to this exact binding (v2.1-prod work); the binding still gives you a recognisable artifact to sign rather than an opaque blob.

upload.title: QES (.p7s)
upload.intro: Upload the file the Diia app produced under «Накласти КЕП». The file is needed for one thing: to prove to the ciphernode committee that you hold a valid individual tax number. The individual tax number itself never leaves your browser in the clear.
upload.headline: Drop your signed .p7s here
upload.hint: or click to choose a file
upload.wrongPrefix: Not a QES — subjectSerial does not start with TINUA-.

passkey.title: Passkey on this device
passkey.intro: We'll create a Passkey with the PRF extension. The authenticator (Face ID, Touch ID, security key) syncs via iCloud / Google / Microsoft, so losing this device doesn't lose your Passkey.
passkey.introEarly: We create the Passkey now, before we touch the ciphernode or the chain. If your authenticator can't deliver a PRF output, nothing is committed anywhere — you can retry on another device with no leftover state.
passkey.recoveryNote: Recovery: Passkey cloud sync only in v2; yearly re-enrollment via Diia from v3 onward.
passkey.created: Passkey created. PRF extension is active.
passkey.unsupported: This browser or device doesn't support WebAuthn PRF. Try Chrome, Safari, or Edge — or a hardware security key with hmac-secret.

done.title: Enrollment complete
done.persisting: Sealing your Passkey-encrypted store on this device…
done.ready: You're enrolled. Ready to sign polls.
done.persistError: Could not write the local store: {{detail}}

oprf.title: Compute the commitment via the ciphernode
oprf.intro: Your browser hashes the individual tax number into a ristretto255 point, blinds it with a random scalar, and sends it to the ciphernode. The committee returns its share plus a DLEQ proof; the browser unblinds and obtains the deterministic 32-byte commitment.
oprf.running: Blinding individual tax number and contacting the ciphernode…
oprf.dleqInvalid: DLEQ proof did not verify — the ciphernode may have returned an incorrect value. Try again.
oprf.pubkeyMismatch: The OPRF server's public key does not match the one pinned in the client. Possible MITM — enrollment aborted.
oprf.ageBlockedHint: Civic Voice is for adult citizens only. You can return when you turn {{min}}.

register.title: Register in the Merkle commitment
register.intro: The ciphernode appends your commitment to the Merkle tree and returns a fresh root together with the ciphernode's attestation signature. The next step records that signature on-chain.
register.alreadyEnrolled: This individual tax number is already enrolled. v2 forbids Sybil — that's the whole point.

chain.title: Record on-chain
chain.intro: Sign `EnrollmentRegistry.updateRoot(newRoot, newCommitments, attesterSig)` with your own wallet. This updates the tree root in the contract — a one-time action per enrollment. You pay the gas yourself.
chain.relayerIntro: We're recording your enrollment on-chain for you. No wallet, no gas, no ETH on your end.
chain.modeNotice: Connecting a wallet links your enrollment to that address on-chain. Skip wallet to enroll privately via relayer.
chain.useWallet: I'd rather submit from my own wallet →
chain.walletConnectHint: QR code for a mobile wallet
chain.wrongChain: Switch your wallet to Ethereum Sepolia.

errors.badSignature: Attester signature does not match the current root.
errors.emptyBatch: Commitment batch is empty — the ciphernode returned no commitments.
errors.notAdmin: Only the admin can perform this action.

done.title: Enrollment complete
done.body: Your commitment is in the tree and your Passkey is bound to this device. You can now sign any open poll in seconds.

vote.title: How do you vote?
vote.missingEnrollment: No enrollment on this device. Run «Enroll», or sign in with the same Apple / Google / Microsoft account if your Passkey is cloud-synced.
vote.alreadyEnrolledElsewhere: I already enrolled on another device →

unlock.title: Unlock your Passkey
unlock.intro: The authenticator returns a PRF output we use to decrypt the OPRF output and the Merkle membership proof from local storage. This is the only moment your browser handles sensitive material.

prove.title: Generate the proof
prove.intro: Your browser computes the ZK proof in ~5–10 seconds. Unlike v1, there's no 30-second RSA check inside the circuit — only a small Merkle membership and a nullifier.

submit.intro: Proof is ready. Submit your vote via the v2 relayer.

errors.NullifierAlreadyUsed: You have already voted on this poll.
errors.InvalidVote: This vote value is not allowed for the poll's mode.

v2.title: v2: Passkey cloud sync only
v2.intro: v2 has exactly one recovery primitive: cloud sync on your Passkey provider. Sign in on a new device with the same Apple / Google / Microsoft account and the Passkey is already there.
v2.point1: If you have cloud sync on, recovery is automatic — no action here.
v2.point2: If you do not have cloud sync and lose every device that holds the Passkey, your v2 enrollment is locked until v3 ships. There is no within-v2 backdoor — every candidate was either a duplicate of what Diia already provides or a new attack surface.

v3.title: v3: yearly re-enrollment via Diia
v3.intro: Recovery in v3 is a property of yearly epoch rotation. Lose everything? Wait for the next epoch, re-authenticate with Diia, and a fresh `s_year` is issued — no separate recovery flow needed. This is the universal recovery primitive across the whole system, the same cadence as state-issued documents (passport renewals, driver's licence renewals). When v3 lands, this page will surface the next renewal date and the one-tap re-enroll prompt.

verify.heading: Identification via QES
verify.subtitle: Verify your identity and prove you are an adult citizen of Ukraine. All personal data always stays only on your device and is never transmitted anywhere.
verify.adultsOnlyDetail: The Diia signature you uploaded is below the {{min}}-year age threshold (resolved to {{found}}).
verify.identifyBody: We use the individual tax number to compute your anonymous identity locally and to cross-check the certificate in your .p7s.
verify.identifyPrivacy: Your individual tax number never reaches the chain. It's hashed and blinded locally; only the blinded value is sent to the OPRF service.
verify.challengeIntro: The file crisp-qes-challenge.txt has been downloaded to this device. Follow the steps below.
challengeSteps: Open the Diia Document Signing website.
Open the Diia app on your phone, tap "Diia Scanner" and scan the QR.
Create the signature in the app.
On the browser page, click "Next", then "No, choose another format".
Select CAdES format. Leave the rest of the fields unchanged.
Sign the file by scanning the QR again with the Diia app.
Click "Download the signed file". The signed file in .p7s format should be saved to your device.
Upload this file here and click "Verify".

verify.dropHint: The .p7s file produced by signing the file above
verify.parsed: QES recognised and individual tax number matches.
verify.verifyingBody: Contacting OPRF · verifying DLEQ · unblinding · submitting to chain.
verify.verifyingWait: This can take 10–20 seconds. Don't close this tab.
verify.verifiedBody: We created your anonymous voting key. It will now be saved on this device and protected by your Passkey — so only you can vote.
verify.verifiedRecoveredBody: This Diia identity is already enrolled this epoch — no new commitment was created. We re-derived your existing anonymous identity from your Diia signature.
verify.savingBody: Waiting for the Passkey prompt, then encrypting.
verify.savedOk: You're verified. You can now vote and create polls.

me.heading: Account
me.subtitle: Local-only. This page lives entirely on this device.
me.notVerifiedBefore: Your Passkey is set up, but you haven't verified with QES yet. You can browse polls, but signing and creating require verification.
me.signedSubtitle: Only you can compute this list. Nobody else — not even us — can link your nullifiers to your identity.
me.noSigned: You haven't signed any poll yet.
me.recoveryBody: Two ways back if you lose access: same device → unlock with your Passkey (instant); new or wiped device → set up a Passkey and re-run Verify with Diia, which restores your existing anonymous identity. Heads-up: Diia recovery needs only your Diia signature, so guard it like your passport. See
me.lockBody: Clears your decrypted signing key from memory. You stay verified on this device — just tap your Passkey next time you sign. Nothing is deleted. Use this when you step away.
me.forgetBody: Wipes your local vault and Passkey reference from this device. Your on-chain enrollment stays — recover later with your QES on any device. Use this on a shared or public computer.

about.heading: About the project
about.disclaimer: Open voting service. Results have no legal consequences and serve as a tool for expressing public opinion.
about.availability: The platform is available to all citizens who have a qualified electronic signature (QES/KEP) — citizens of Ukraine and 27 European Union countries under the eIDAS regulation.
about.body: Civic Voice was created so that every citizen can freely express their position — anonymously, privately, and with a guarantee that their vote will be counted fairly. We combine state identification (QES) with zero-knowledge cryptography so that nobody — neither the organizer, nor the platform, nor any third party — can find out who voted and how. Results are available to everyone in a public distributed registry (blockchain), where they cannot be changed, deleted, or falsified. The project's code is open — anyone can verify that the system works exactly as stated.
about.techIntro: Civic Voice is the first solution that combines state electronic identification (QES) with zero-knowledge proofs and homomorphic encryption for conducting civic polls. For the first time, a citizen can confirm their uniqueness via their tax ID (IPN) without revealing it to anyone — not the platform, not the blockchain, not even Diia. One person — one vote, mathematically guaranteed, with no way to find out who voted and how.
about.techStack: Noir (ZK proofs) · VOPRF (RFC 9497) · Solidity/Foundry (Ethereum) · CRISP/FHE (encrypted tally) · QES integration
about.transparencyTitle: What data goes to the registry
about.tech1body: A qualified electronic signature that every Ukrainian already has. Confirms citizenship and adulthood — without transmitting personal data.
about.tech2body: A zero-knowledge proof confirms you have the right to vote without revealing who you are. Created on your device in 10 seconds.
about.tech3body: Blockchain infrastructure is stored in a distributed public registry. Results are verifiable by anyone — without a server owner.
about.tech4body: All code is open. Open source means the ability to verify. And even better — to look at how it works, choose what to choose — and change more.
about.team1desc: Idea, concept and system developer: architecture, ZK circuits and registry smart contract.
about.team2role: PhD Student, NaUKMA, Theory of Law
about.team2desc: Idea, concept and site design developer. Dissertation research topic: "Network consensus as a source of law".
